svg.text: Where each control acts: Sprint 5 along a request's path
NGINX runs a request through fixed phases. A refusal ends the request in the phase where it happens,
so the order below decides what a client sees and which checks it costs you.
An L4 load balancer can send the client address in the PROXY header.
The timeout is a total. limit_conn can't see a slowloris client yet.
$remote_addr becomes the real client, for every check below and the log.
Refused before any limit zone sees the client: 20 of 20 got 403.
Checked against Content-Length, before a byte of the body is read.
A location that returns is answered here and never reaches the limits.
Counted before allow/deny. limit_req can also delay instead of refusing.
First match wins. A denied flood got 6 x 403 and 14 x 429 (PREACCESS first).
The body timeout is a gap between reads. A slow upload holds a limit_conn slot.
limit_rate is per connection: pair it with limit_conn.
Dry run shows up here as REJECTED_DRY_RUN while the request passes.
An idle connection is closed; the next request on it starts over.
Refuse as early as you can
A refusal ends the request in its phase.
they never touch the limit zones.
realip runs in POST_READ, so geo, the
limits, allow/deny and the log all see the
client, if you trust only your own proxies.
geo, map and keyval run only when a phase
reads them. One tier table feeds keys,
rates and blocks in every phase.
Counts quoted were measured in the Sprint 5 lab on nginx 1.31.6; the side quest on NGINX Plus R37.1.1.
